title: The Friendship Formula
heading: The Friendship Formula

sourceRefs.role: bounded support for intensity through nonverbal signals
secondary cross-support for friend-signal concepts used in intensity discussion

coreClaim: Schafer presents friendship as a function of four controllable variables: proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity.
distinctMechanism: The formula treats relationships as dynamic systems that can be strengthened, diagnosed, or cooled by changing exposure, time, and emotional quality.
requiredAnchors: The formula itself: Friendship = Proximity x (Frequency + Duration) x Intensity.
Proximity matters only when exposure happens in a nonthreatening environment.
Intensity comes through verbal and nonverbal behavior and acts like the glue that makes the other variables matter.
specificApplications: Audit a stale friendship or partnership.
Improve a promising relationship by changing one variable on purpose.
Reduce an unwanted relationship gradually by lowering the variables.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard depth must show that the same variables can also deepen harmful influence or manipulative attachment, so the model is descriptive and strategic rather than morally self-validating.
thresholdQuestion: Where is the line between consciously shaping relationship conditions and engineering someone else's attachment?
